reason: The text describes Hebrew midwives (Shifrah and Puah) who resist the Egyptian Pharaoh's command to kill Hebrew male infants. Rather than being antagonistic to their people, these Hebrew leaders show protective compassion by preserving Hebrew lives. The midwives 'feared God and did not do as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the male children alive' (וַתִּירֶאן הַמְיַלְּדוֹת אֶת־ הָאֱלֹהִים וְלֹא עָשׂוּ). They are rewarded by God for their actions. The only antagonistic force toward the Hebrew people in this passage is Pharaoh, not the Hebrew leaders.
